model_reported.name: conduire-experience-optimisation
model_reported.summary: Combined the retained SSE2 prefix with the word-scanned suffix, preserving strict UTF-8 checks, bounded reads, and the run ABI.

model_reported.name: inspecter-environnement
model_reported.summary: Kept the existing __SSE2__ guard and unaligned SSE2 load; introduced no additional ISA assumption, and the suffix also has a portable word-scan path.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique
model_reported.summary: No new version-specific API or ISA feature is introduced; this reuses the supplied SSE2 intrinsics and standard memcpy.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Used prior measured means only to frame the comparison; the integration remains unmeasured and requires official correctness and timing evaluation.

proposal.hypothesis: The 16-byte SSE2 prefix scan can skip long initial ASCII runs, while the 8-byte word checks after the first mixed vector may skip later complete ASCII blocks that scalar suffix decoding would inspect byte by byte. The additional masks and mixed-block decoding may instead cost more on short or dense non-ASCII inputs. The combined program is unmeasured and must beat the parent's 39.978 µs mean; no additive gain is assumed.

retained: Retained the bounded 16-byte SSE2 ASCII-prefix scan and its handoff at the first vector containing a high-bit byte.
Replaced scalar suffix processing with an 8-byte high-bit mask loaded using memcpy; decode mixed blocks by complete code point through the block boundary, then validate the bounded scalar tail.
Preserved the UTF-8 validity rules, run ABI, output, and conditional SSE2 compilation.
